topic: sub:12|Relative frequency and probability|Relative and expected frequency

7725.stem: Two fair dice are thrown, and the results are recorded.

parts.latex: What is the probability of 3 and 4 in that order?
What is the probability of throwing a double (the same number on both dice)?
What is the expected frequency of throwing a ‘double 5’ or a ‘double 6’ if the dice are thrown 180 times?

solutions.latex:
There are 6 doubles among 36 equally likely outcomes.
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{double}) &= \dfrac{6}{36} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{6} \end{aligned}$$

There are two favourable outcomes (double 5 or double 6) out of 36, so the probability is $\dfrac{2}{36}$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Expected frequency} &= \dfrac{2}{36} \times 180 \\ &= 10 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Expected frequency} = 10$$
criteria: Correctly determines the probability $\dfrac{2}{36}$, or equivalent merit
